recipes.name: Best Hot Crab Dip
ingredients_raw: 2 (8 ounce) cans artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
0.5 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon dried dill, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon Old Bay Seasoning TM, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8x8-inch square baking pan.

In a large bowl, combine crabmeat, sour cream, cream cheese, buttermilk, mayonnaise, Monterey Jack cheese, Cheddar cheese, capers, artichoke hearts, garlic, black pepper, and dill. Stir until well mixed. Spoon dip into prepared baking pan. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and Old Bay Seasoning.
Bake in preheated oven until top is crusty, about 15 to 20 minutes.

Cut the top off the loaf of bread. Hollow out the loaf and cube the top and the removed pieces so that they may be used for dipping. Spoon hot dip into hollow bread loaf. Serve immediately with bread pieces for dipping.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Hot Crab Dip
raw_recipe.description: The name says it all. The best hot crab dip recipe, creamy with cheese, flavored with capers and artichoke hearts, and served in a bread bowl.

review.reviewBody: The first time I made it, I [accidentally] left our the Buttermilk. The second time I made it I wished that I had forgotten the Buttermilk; it was much better without it. Next time I make it I will add more crab meat and more artichoke hearts, for a thicker, heartier dip.

This was an awful dip...Thank goodness I did a trial run...when I took it out of the oven there were pools of oil on the top and sides...too many fatty ingredients? there were unmixed lumps of cream cheese in various cooked pockets although I had stirred thoroughly...the cream cheese should have been beaten with the other ingredients with heavy duty mix master after softened? the capers were overwhelming in taste...they should have been finely diced? the garlic was overwhelming...maybe 1 tablespoon vs. 2? You should only use fresh crab meat...the canned taste was unmistakable (I thought that with all the yummy sounding ingredients the canned taste would cook out)

Very good recipe with a few modifications: * I cut the recipe in half (because it was just a lot of dip) * Even after cutting it in half, I still only used about a half pound of fresh crab meat (1lb was just way too much!) *I omitted the capers just because the recipe tasted great with out them - however if you were to add them I would drastically cut them - by half or more. * I also halved the amount of artichokes (again by at least half). *I also omitted the buttermilk - it was great with out it * I also cut the mayo in half. * Lastly I added a teaspoon of crushed red pepper and doubled the old bay seasoning. Tossed it all in a crock pot and VOILA - it was great!

I made this for a party and it was fabulous. I took the advise of others and did not use capers and only one half of a can of artichoke hearts, chopped very well. I bought two containers of lump crab meat in the refrigerated section and it was very expensive. Next time I will buy the back fin because of all the other ingredients it would not have mattered. I probably tripled the old bay and dill. I also used my potato masher to get the lumps out of the cream cheese. It made a lot. I took it to a party of 22 and brought half of it home, however it warmed up nicely in the microwave. I would make this again for a large party. Oh and I heated it up in a pottery pie dish and use baguette bread for dipping.

This dish is very creamy. I'm not a huge fan of capers, and only added 2 T to add that level of flavor. The cheddar cheese isn't necessary, and I'd probably reduce the amount of mayo in the future. I would add more parmesan cheese and Old Bay if I remake again. A couple dashes of sherry and cayenne pepper might taste good too. I used real snow crab leg meat.

I'd make this again... was a little hesitant for all the strong flavor but with the right adjustments this was well received. I cut back the garlic to one clove and the capers wayyyy back to one two tbsp or so, they're not my favorite flavor but wanted to give the taste a try. I will admit the capers compliment the artichoke flavor nicely. I think the big difference was using gruyere in place of the cheddar, its a less oily cheese with more bite. People gave it high stars and with my kitchenaid mixer it was very easy. Was excellent with tortilla chips. The recipe makes a lot of dip.

I made this New Years eve. I added all lump crab, all the cheeses, mayonnaise and sour cream. I cut the capers back to 1 Tbsp. Chopped. I only used approximately 8 oz. Artichoke hearts chopped. I cut back on garlic to 1 Tbsp., 1/2 tsp. pepper, 1 tsp. dried dill, 1 tsp. Old bay. I did make an addition of 1 tsp. dried mustard, 1 tsp. worsetershire sauce. And 1 Tbsp. Dry sherry. I looked at all the reviews before diving in, and with the tweaking all of my guests raved about this!

I made the mistake of using Trader Joe's canned crab meat because I heard it was good (I am near Dallas). ONLY use fresh crab for this recipe. I omitted the buttermilk but next time will use. I used 1 can of artichokes because of negative reviews; however that amount was lost in the rest of the ingredients - next time will use 2 cans. The non-pareils were an excellent touch. The recipe calls for an 8" x 8" square pan. This is a mistake. I needed a 4 quart bowl to bake this in.

I was eager to try this recipe after reading the ingredient list. I just so happened to have some shrimp and crab legs leftover from last night's seafood boil. So no canned crab for us. This was so yummy and flavorful. I decided to not use the capers and only used 1/2 cup of artichokes. I did add onion powder and chopped spinach. Awesome with tortillas chips.Definitely making this again!

Everyone loved it! Took others' suggestions and made it without the buttermilk, 2/3 cup of capers, double the Old Bay. Was addictive hot or cold. Went well with tortilla chips and/or crackers as I didn't go the bread bowl route.

Oh. My. Goodness. This is the best crab dip ever. I made it last fall and it was a huge hit. Today I made it and pumped up the volume on the spices. 1 full teaspoon dill and 1/2 teaspoon Old Bay went into the mix, another 1/2 teaspoon Old Bay sprinkled on top. Also added a few dashes of cayenne. (And I never add buttermilk, I like my dip a little thick) I bake in a casserole dish and dip with crusty artisan breads. PS I have the strangest (pregnancy induced) aversion to garlic ---so I halved the minced garlic for this recipe and it still turned out amazing.
I made it to serve 9. It was good but very greasy. I’ll try low fat items next time. Also I will add less capers. It took 30 min in my oven.
awesome
Wonderful

Makes far too much dip, and I was not thrilled with the results. It isn't bad, but nothing I'd recommend or make again. I used fresh Dungeness crab, which is very expensive, and was wonderful by itself, but it was a waste putting it into a dip.
I make this every year as part of our Christmas feast, my adult children request it without fail. I don't change a thing, it's perfect as is, thank you for the yummy recipe!
Presented well but, as other reviewers noted, it had too much liquid. I would not make it again.
Made it to the recipe and it was wonderful. I used King crab and may have put in a little more than the recipe called for but you can't go wrong with more crab.

The recipe calls for an 8" x 8" square pan. This is a mistake. I needed a 4 quart bowl to bake this in.

So terrible that I made an account just to leave this review. I'm a displaced Northeasterner, and I decided to give this recipe a try for a potluck.

I am a chef by trade and have made crab and artichoke dip many times; I was looking for something a bit different and opted for this recipe on account of the capers and buttermilk.

After $50 of ingredients and the better part of an hour, I decided to toss the filling and at least save the sourdough.

I followed this recipe to the letter, and my advice to others is this: there are plenty of other great crab dip recipes out there - steer clear of this one.
